newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to hike tortilla prices next month - radio.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to hike tortilla prices next month - radio.

text.p: Mexico's government has agreed to increase controlled tortilla prices to 2.50 pesos per kilo from the current limit of 1.70 per kilo, radio network Radio Red said Wednesday.
Citing unnamed sources from the National Corn Flour and Tortilla Producers' Chamber, Radio Red said the increase would be effective from next month. No specific date was given.
Tortillas, corn flour pancakes eaten more widely than bread, are one of the few food products with price controls still in place in Mexico.

The government has been moving to erase price controls to move to a fully market-oriented economy. But because the food is an important element in the consumer price index, there has been reluctance to increase prices so as not to cause an inflation spike.

Members of the chamber have been pressing for a price hike or for controls to be lifted in recent days. They have threatened to boycott a government scheme that gives free tortillas to the poorest of Mexican families.
